title: Criteria API
mediaType: Not applicable — the Criteria API is a Java object-graph API for building queries programmatically; it has no serialized wire format.

sources.title: Chapter 32: Introduction to the Java Persistence API

expressiveness.rationale: Builds SQL-like queries programmatically with joins, subqueries, aggregate and group-by expressions, and dynamic predicate composition, though more verbose to write than an equivalent JPQL string.

simplicity.rationale: The type-safe, fluent-builder style requires generated metamodel classes and verbose Java code for even simple queries, a steeper learning curve than writing a JPQL/SQL string directly.

flexibility.rationale: Like JPQL, it operates over a fixed, annotated object-relational entity schema and is not designed for dynamic or schema-less data.

communityAndEcosystem.rationale: Part of the same widely-adopted Jakarta Persistence specification as JPQL, implemented by Hibernate, EclipseLink and OpenJPA, with mature documentation and IDE tooling for the generated metamodel.

extensibility.rationale: Supports custom expressions and generic function calls similar to JPQL, but the API surface itself is fixed by the specification.

transportCompatibility.rationale: Exists only as an in-process Java API for building queries; has no notion of URL or HTTP transport.

standardization.rationale: Formally part of the Jakarta Persistence specification (JSR 317/338), implemented independently by multiple ORM vendors.

security.rationale: Queries are built entirely from typed Java objects and bound parameters rather than string concatenation, making it structurally resistant to injection by construction.

performance.rationale: Translated to native SQL by the JPA provider with the same caching/optimization characteristics as JPQL; the type-safe API adds no runtime cost beyond query construction.

orthogonality.rationale: Predicates and expressions compose fluently as Java objects, but the API's verbosity and reliance on generated metamodel classes add indirection compared to a plain query string.

summary: The JPA Criteria API is a type-safe, programmatic alternative to JPQL that is structurally immune to injection by construction and formally standardized alongside it, but its fluent, metamodel-driven style trades away the simplicity of writing plain query strings and, like JPQL, is confined to in-process Java use over a fixed entity schema.

example.scenario: Retrieve products where category = "electronics" and price > 100, sorted by price descending, page 2 of 10 per page.
